title: Multilang embeddings dataset curation + smoke regression report
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for curating a multilingual embeddings evaluation set and recording a quick smoke regression after swapping embedding model candidates. Goal: produce a small, high-signal dataset we can run nightly to detect obvious regressions in semantic search relevance and clustering sanity across languages (EN, ES, DE, FR, JA, and pt-BR).

Scope and constraints:
- Keep the dataset small (~1.5k doc fragments, ~300 queries) for fast runs (under 10m).
- Mix of short queries (1–4 tokens), natural language questions, and long contextual prompts (multi-sentence).
- Cover verticals: docs (how-tos), product descriptions, support tickets, code snippets, and short news blurbs.
- Include intentionally challenging negatives (near-duplicates, paraphrases, topical drift).
- Prioritize practical signal for RAG and search: top-k recall and clustering sanity are most important.

Dataset composition (target counts):
- Documents: 1,500 total across languages. Approx per-lang split: EN 500, ES 250, DE 200, FR 200, JA 200, pt-BR 150.
- Queries: 300 total (mix of search queries and question-style queries). Each query mapped to 3–8 relevant doc ids (graded relevance 0/1/2).
- Hard negatives: ~1,000 query-doc pairs flagged as hard negative (paraphrase but not relevant).

Sampling sources (notes):
- Public docs + internal synthetic prompts: product pages, help center articles, and anonymized support snippets (redacted).
- Translate high-quality English queries to other languages (back-translate for validation). Avoid machine-only translation for ground truth — run a human spot check for 30% of translated pairs.
- Use code-comment snippets from GH examples for code-search-like queries in EN/DE/FR.

Annotation scheme (simple to compute):
- Relevance: 2 = gold (direct answer/contains exact info), 1 = partial/helpful, 0 = not relevant.
- Each query has at least 1 label==2.
- Store annotations as flat CSV: query_id, query_text, doc_id, doc_text_snippet, relevance, lang.

Evaluation metrics (smoke-run):
- Retrieval: Recall@1, Recall@5, MRR@10, NDCG@10 (compute per-language + macro average).
- Clustering: For a small sampling (200 docs per lang), compute silhouette score on kmeans(k=20) using embeddings; also compute Davies-Bouldin index and manual spot-check of cluster labels.
- Stability/regression: cosine-similarity shift distribution between baseline and candidate on 10k random doc pairs. Flag if median shift > 0.02 (absolute) or if >5% pairs flip relative ordering for top-k.

Quick-run checklist (smoke):
- [ ] Prepare doc CSV, query CSV, annotation CSV (head checks).
- [ ] Generate baseline embeddings (model: embed-v1.2) for docs and queries.
- [ ] Generate candidate embeddings (model: embed-v2-quant) for same items.
- [ ] Compute retrieval metrics baseline vs candidate.
- [ ] Compute clustering metrics and run small t-SNE visualizations for manual spot-check.
- [ ] Produce regression summary and triage list.

Observed smoke-run (example output from 2025-02-17 run):
- Baseline: embed-v1.2, Candidate: embed-v2-quant (8-bit).
- Retrieval (macro averages across langs):
  - Recall@1: baseline 0.44, candidate 0.40 (drop 0.04)
  - Recall@5: baseline 0.78, candidate 0.76 (drop 0.02)
  - MRR@10: baseline 0.61, candidate 0.58 (drop 0.03)
  - NDCG@10: baseline 0.72, candidate 0.69 (drop 0.03)
- Per-lang highlights:
  - EN: R@1 0.51 -> 0.48 (small drop)
  - JA: R@1 0.37 -> 0.30 (noticeable drop, investigate tokenization/segmentation)
  - ES/pt-BR: minimal change (~0.01)
- Clustering sanity (sampled test, 200 docs/lang):
  - Silhouette: baseline 0.28, candidate 0.23 (lower suggests clusters blurred)
  - Davies-Bouldin: baseline 1.34, candidate 1.62 (worse)
  - Manual spot-check: several Japanese product description clusters merged with unrelated short-news docs — possible embedding collapse on CJK short text.
- Stability: median cosine shift (doc vs doc) = -0.015 (small), but top-k ordering flips >7% for JA queries.

Initial hypotheses and triage directions:
1) Quantization artifacts affecting languages with short token sequences (JA), or models using different tokenization/embedding tables. Check if candidate uses different tokenizer preproc step.
2) Embedding norm collapse for short docs under quantized model. Inspect per-length norm distribution.
3) Candidate kernel selection or pooling change (mean vs CLS). Confirm pooling strategy identical.
4) Training/objective differences — check model card for multilingual coverage; candidate might deprioritize some locales.

Quick debugging steps (next actions):
- Re-run embeddings for JA with additional context windows (append 1–2 sentence padding) to test short-text sensitivity.
- Compute per-lang embedding L2 norm distributions (plot) and compare baseline vs candidate.
- Generate synthetic near-duplicates for JA and test nearest neighbors stability.
- If quantization suspected, run candidate with float fallback (if available) on a 200-doc JA subset.
- Add logging to detect if sentencepiece/hug-tokenizer variant mismatches occur in preproc pipeline.

Annotation gaps / TODOs for dataset quality:
- Need human spot-check for 30% of translated relevance labels (assigned to Zoe/Karen).
- Increase technical docs proportion for DE and FR (currently thin).
- Add 50 negative paraphrase pairs for each non-EN language.

Longer-term improvements (post-smoke):
- Expand dataset to 10k docs and integrate into CI with weekly runs and automated alerting if R@1 drops >2 points or silhouette < 0.20.
- Add model-versioned expected metrics in our SLO dashboard (console: embeddings/regressions).
- Build small web UI for manual cluster inspection with language filter and query-driven neighbor lists.

Notes to reviewers / context: 
- This doc is intentionally scrappy — the goal is reproducible, actionable checks that engineers can run quickly before approving a model candidate for production.
- If you run the pipeline, paste the main metric table into the PR and add screenshots of a couple of t-SNE views (EN and JA).

Example sample entries (CSV-friendly snippets):
- query_id: Q-EN-001, query_text: "how to reset api key", lang: en, expected_doc_ids: [D-EN-123, D-EN-9], notes: "FAQ and tutorial should be top hits"
- query_id: Q-JA-042, query_text: "APIキー 再発行 方法", lang: ja, expected_doc_ids: [D-JA-88], notes: "single step answer in support blurb"
- doc_id: D-PT-17, doc_text_snippet: "Como redefinir a chave de API em 3 passos", lang: pt-BR

Owner and contact: Priya Patel (priya@redwood.ai). Ping in #eng-applied-ml for urgent regressions.

Changelog (working):
- 2025-02-10 created initial dataset sketch
- 2025-02-14 added per-lang sampling targets and annotation scheme
- 2025-02-17 ran smoke comparison between embed-v1.2 and embed-v2-quant; recorded preliminary metrics and triage notes
- 2025-02-18 appended debugging steps and updated TODOs
